text:
DeployBot: :rotating_light: Deploy started: region=eu-west, deployment=green-v2 -> traffic ramp to 20% canary at 2025-08-12T10:02Z. Rollout ID: r-20250812-eu-g2
Anna (oncall): seeing elevated 502s from customers in EU, starting ~10:05. Alerting X-Proxy error spikes.
Raj: copying. Which cluster/edge is reporting this?
Katie: logs show backend-pool-eu-west-2 returning 502s with KV cache misses. Sample log: `2025-08-12T10:04:58Z ERROR upstream 502 GET /v1/generate  x-request-id=...`
Mike: traffic graph — backend error rate jumped from 0.3% -> 7% for green-v2 canary, blue stable is fine. Latency also +120ms p50.
Anna (oncall): PagerDuty page: P12345 triggered at 10:06 for EU-canary-high-5xx. @PagerDuty please escalate to SRE.
PagerDuty: Paging SRE: urgent: eu-west canary 5xx spike (P12345). Oncall: Anna (oncall).
SRE-Bot: Incident created: INC-2025-08-12-eu-canary. Runbooks: check deploy health, traffic split, DNS.
Raj: quick hypothesis — partial DNS weight propagation meant some EU edge nodes still resolving green-v2 to the new origin which hasn't warmed caches -> 502s. Need to verify DNS weights and edge mapping.
Katie: confirmed: control-plane shows geo-weight for eu-west split to green=20% but DNS entries for some PoPs still returning green CNAMEs due to 300s TTL; edge pool IPs include some that point to a new origin subset missing a migration flag.
Sara: customer reports: several embeddings/generation failures via hosted API from EU customers. We're seeing retries escalate cost.
Anna (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) Pause rollout (stop ramp), 2) set kill-switch to route entire traffic back to blue stable (roll back traffic), 3) notify impacted customers. Thoughts?
Theo: agree. Pause ramp first. Command: `redwood deploy pause --id r-20250812-eu-g2` (internal).
Mike: paused. Deploy system: `status: paused` at 10:12 UTC.
Katie: can't toggle TTLs remotely for all DNS caches. Let's prefer a traffic-level kill-switch so clients hitting entrypoints are routed to blue.
Raj: applying kill-switch now: `curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer <secret>' https://control-plane.internal/api/v1/rollouts/r-20250812-eu-g2/kill`
SRE-Bot: Kill-switch applied by Raj at 10:14:12Z. Rollout traffic routed -> blue stable.
DeployBot: Rollout r-20250812-eu-g2: traffic weight -> green=0%, blue=100%.
Anna (oncall): monitoring metrics... 502s falling. p95 latency back to baseline by 10:16.
Sara: started a customer message draft for support: "We observed elevated errors for EU customers during a regional canary. Routing has been reverted and we’re monitoring. We’ll follow up with timeline and root cause."
Mike: interestingly, a subset of IPs continued to see errors for ~3 more minutes — likely due to DNS TTL caching at external resolvers. Confirming by tracing IPs: `edge-ip 34.200.x.y` which still pointed to green origin until caches expired.
Katie: added temporary WAF rule to reject traffic to the new origin IPs from edge for 15 mins to reduce error propagation.
Raj: started controlled rollback undo steps for green-v2 in eu-west. We're going to mark this rollout as failed and block immediate re-ramp until RC review.
Anna (oncall): PagerDuty: please update status as acknowledged -> actioned -> mitigated.
PagerDuty: P12345 status updated: mitigated at 10:18 UTC.
SRE-Bot: Post-mitigations checklist: collect logs (edge, origin), DNS query traces, rollout config, and customer impact window.
Sara: customers impacted list (prelim): 12 orgs, predominantly EU latency-sensitive apps. Estimating 2-3 minutes of errors during peak depending on resolver TTLs.
Theo: question for follow-up: why did feature flag/origin gate not flip for green-v2 in some origin pool members? That would explain mismatch between control-plane and origin.
Katie: found one origin subset missing Docker env var `FEATURE_GATE_PREFETCH=true` in the green group; that caused cache-miss storm and upstream 502s.
Raj: root cause draft: incomplete migration of origin pool config + DNS TTL causing partial exposure of unready origin -> canary failures.
Anna (oncall): current tasks: 1) start incident timeline doc, 2) gather all edge logs and DNS traces, 3) freeze rollout for green-v2, 4) schedule RCA meeting. Assigning: Raj (config/origin checks), Katie (edge/DNS traces), Mike (metrics dashboard + billing impact), Sara (customer comms).
Raj: taking the lead for config fixes. I'll do handoff when I go offline at 18:00.
Anna (oncall): thanks — I'm staying on to ensure we have a clean incident doc. If anyone else reads: react with :thumbsup: when tasks accepted.
Mike: accepted task. :thumbsup:
Katie: accepted. collecting traces now.
Sara: will send the initial customer note to the support thread and escalate for those 12 orgs.
SRE-Bot: Incident INC-2025-08-12-eu-canary updated: severity -> Sev2.
Anna (oncall): summary for execs (to paste): "Brief: During a regional blue/green canary in eu-west, partial origin config drift combined with DNS TTL propagation led to ~12 customer failures and transient 5xx spike. Mitigation: paused rollout, applied kill-switch routing to blue stable, additional WAF temporary rule; incident mitigated at 10:18 UTC. Next: RCAs and deploy gating improvements."
Raj: leaving a note about follow-ups: add automated preflight to validate origin env parity and post-deploy end-to-end synthetic checks in each PoP before any traffic ramp >0%.
Anna (oncall): handing off to Raj for config remediation. Raj oncall period now.
Raj: taking over the incident thread and ownership for remediation.
DeployBot: Deploy logs archived: s3://redwood-incidents/INC-2025-08-12-eu-canary/logs.tar.gz
Anna (oncall): thanks everyone — closing Slack coordination. We'll reconvene in RCA.
Sara: will post customer follow-up once RCAs finalize.
